C1.worst_defect: On a phone the header shows only "Docs" and "Live demo"; "Quick start" and "At the till" (the pages an owner needs: can staff sell, how do I close the day) are hidden behind a chevron, and the hero never says in plain words that a shop owner needs their developer for setup.

C2.worst_defect: The phone hero shows the till running in a phone layout (Products / Cart tabs), but "Before you start" says "tablets and phones, an iPad included, are not tested yet". That is a mixed signal for an owner choosing a counter device.

C3.worst_defect: For a developer the path is complete, but the device-key role a till uses "has the step 4 permissions except ReadOrder, so add ReadOrder to that role yourself". A freelancer can miss this, and the till's order history is then refused on day one (the changelog repeats it as "Not in the release notes").
C3.where: quick-start "Optional: a device key"; changelog.desktop.01 0.2.0 last bullet

C4.worst_defect: Troubleshooting mixes counter guidance with SuperAdmin GraphQL (tallyNeedsAdminCommands, tallyResolveNeedsAdmin, the errorCode list) on one page, so a cashier between customers can't quickly find the part meant for them; "Any other code: the till has no retry or skip" is a dead end for a non-developer.

C5.worst_defect: The cashier-sheet and closure screenshots sit inside an oversized grey outer frame with large empty padding (a frame within a frame at about 60% width), unlike the full-width payment screenshot on the same page.

C6.worst_defect: The pages are very long on a phone (quick-start 10580 px, at-the-till about 9200 px). "Count the drawer and close the day" is at the bottom of a long scroll, and the collapsed "On this page" dropdown is the only way to jump there. There is no overflow, and tables collapse well.

C7.worst_defect: Home ships 51 KiB of unused JavaScript and 150 ms of render-blocking resources (LCP 2.3 s). Everything else is clean: llms.txt, sitemap, JSON-LD, search API and a 404 that returns 404.

overall_worst.defect: On a real store a till refund can't be finished by the shop: "No, not on plugin 0.3.0: refund in the Vendure Dashboard. The refund stays Pending until an administrator settles it with two Admin API calls". For every refund the owner has to call their freelance developer, and the docs give no non-developer way to settle it.
overall_worst.where: home.desktop.02 "Live demo or your own store" refund row; limitations.desktop.01
overall_worst.fix: Give owners a no-code way to settle POS refunds (a Dashboard action, or a one-page "refund a till sale" checklist an owner can follow), and say in the home table what staff do at the counter meanwhile (Pay out cash / refund on the card terminal), linking to that checklist.
